summary: Post-v0.3.1 release-candidate final-verification phase (bounded; no publication). Re-derived 2Y's frozen release-candidate scope and full capability/supported-agent matrices directly from source (not copied from prose), confirming both accurate. Bumped canonical version from 0.3.0 to 0.3.1 in both identified version sources (pyproject.toml, src/pcae/__init__.py; no other static or generated version location found), verified via pcae runtime inspect --json. Independently found, via fresh live-CLI reproduction rather than code reading alone, that 2Y's own malformed-agent-lock repair was incomplete: well-formed JSON decoding to a non-dict value (array/string/number/bool/null) still crashed both the packaged pcae intake from-files CLI command and, more severely, pcae session bootstrap (the primary session-entry command) with an uncaught AttributeError -- read_agent_lock does not raise for valid-but-wrong-type JSON, so the crash occurred one line later at AgentLock.agent_id, outside 2Y's try/except entirely. Repaired at the root cause (AgentLock.agent_id property, src/pcae/core/agent.py) plus an explicit type check in derive_producer_provenance (src/pcae/core/intake.py) for a clearer rejection reason at that call site, preserving 2Y's own do-not-silently-broaden-fallback discipline (treated as rejection, not silent acceptance). Every affected caller now fails closed deterministically -- pcae session bootstrap becomes a controlled ValueError ('Agent lock already held by .'), already caught cleanly by existing error handling, exit 1, no traceback, no repository mutation. Added 22 fresh tests for the new repair; re-ran 2Y's own 9 tests and the 274-test targeted 2X/2X.1/2W/2W.1/2U.2-4/review/promotion regression, all passing. Promoted pcae intake from-files to docs/QUICKSTART_V0_3.md's primary golden path per 2Y's own deferred recommendation, demoting the legacy Claude Code adapter script to a clearly marked reference footnote; updated the deny-demo section for consistency; audited README.md/CHANGELOG.md/release docs and found no misleading Codex-Ox execution claim. Authored docs/RELEASE_NOTES_V0_3_1.md following the established v0.3.0 release-notes structure. Built wheel (466 files, matching 2Y's own local count) and sdist (472 entries) from the exact clean committed release-candidate commit (5d7edef9), both correctly reporting 0.3.1 in filename and metadata, scanned clean of any private-research/article/secret/env content. Computed SHA-256 checksums directly from the built artifacts. Ran full clean-environment installed-wheel and installed-sdist smokes in two independent disposable venvs against two independent disposable Git repositories -- bootstrap, intake from-files, intake show/list, no-lock with explicit producer, no-lock without producer (clean rejection), codex-ox bootstrap/provenance, and out-of-scope rejection across three distinct producer identities -- with zero external network or AI-service calls at any point and identical behavior between wheel and sdist. Independently re-confirmed producer-identity authority non-flow: equivalent in-scope and out-of-scope submissions from claude-local, codex-ox, and an arbitrary no-lock producer all yield identical execution_allowed=False/promotion_executed=False authority outcomes. Established the clean-committed regression baseline this phase's own instructions required: 4686 targeted tests passing across four suites with zero failures, plus an independent Fast Green A/B run via a real git worktree pinned to the immediately-prior commit (not a dirty-tree comparison) -- 3 new node IDs found, each individually investigated in isolation rather than inheriting any prior phase's classification: one is a concurrent-load artifact that passes cleanly alone, one is an expected until-push guard test that will resolve once this phase's commits are pushed, and one reproduces the exact resource-sensitive subprocess-timeout mechanism 2X.1 and 2Y both independently documented, unrelated to this phase's own diff. Zero attributable regressions. tasks/DONE.md sync debt reconfirmed at 129 warnings, unchanged, repository-maintainer-only. Re-confirmed stable-tag isolation (v0.3.0 dereferences to the same commit SHA as phase entry and origin, no v0.3.1 tag exists, no GitHub Release created, no artifact uploaded, article and private research repository both independently confirmed untouched by filesystem timestamp). Produced a publication checklist and a release-blocker table with zero unresolved BLOCKING or MUST-FIX items -- the one new finding this phase itself surfaced (the wrong-type-JSON lock crash) was repaired and independently re-verified within this same phase, not deferred. Does not publish v0.3.1: no tag, no GitHub Release, no artifact upload, no PyPI action, no modification to v0.3.0 or the article. Recommends exactly one narrow follow-up publication phase requiring separate explicit human authorization.
